transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Smith, I'm here because I'm just completely worn out. It's... it's like even just walking from the bedroom to the kitchen feels like I've been hauling lumber all day. And it doesn't matter how much I rest or sleep, I just never get any energy back. I'm just exhausted all the time.
Have you been feeling consistently sad, hopeless, or uninterested in the things you usually enjoy for most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah. Pretty much every single day. I wake up with this heavy, hopeless feeling right in my chest. It's just... there, right from the start of the day. And some days, I'll just go sit out in the garage and cry. I don't even really know what started it half the time, to be honest. But yeah, it's a constant thing.
Have you experienced similar periods of feeling this low and exhausted in the past, perhaps years ago or at different times in your life?

No, I don't think so. I mean... I've had normal bad days or felt tired in the past, sure, but nothing like this. I've never felt this completely drained and down before. So, no, this is really the first time it's ever been this bad.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your weight since this started?

No, not really. I mean, I guess I'm eating about the same as I always do. I haven't exactly been stepping on the scale lately, but my clothes still fit the same, so... my weight probably hasn't changed. I'm still just eating my regular meals for the most part.
Are you having any trouble falling asleep at night, or are you waking up much earlier than you intend to?

No, I haven't really had any trouble with that. I usually fall asleep just fine once I actually go to bed. And I'm not waking up super early or anything like that. My sleep has been... pretty much normal, I guess.
When you do manage to exert yourself, even with small tasks, do you notice that your symptoms of fatigue and exhaustion get significantly worse for hours or days afterward?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean, I'm always exhausted, so it's hard to tell if doing a small task makes it worse. It's just a constant feeling of being drained, whether I try to do something or just sit there. So, I wouldn't say doing things makes it significantly worse for days afterward, no. It's just... always bad.
Have you noticed if other people have commented that you seem to be moving or speaking much more slowly than usual, or conversely, that you seem restless and unable to sit still?

Yeah, people have definitely brought that up. I'm not restless at all, it's really the opposite. Everything I do has just... slowed down. It feels like my body is moving through mud most of the time. 

And it's not just moving around, it's talking, too. Like, when someone asks me something, I can hear the question just fine, but... I don't know, it just takes me a really long time to actually get the words out to answer them. I just can't seem to speed any of it up.

Have you been experiencing any strange or unusual thoughts, such as feeling like you're being watched or that people are out to get you, or have you been seeing or hearing things that aren't actually there?

Yes, I have. I don't feel like anyone is out to get me or watching me, but... I am hearing things. 

It usually happens when my wife is at work and the house is completely quiet. I hear voices, and it's as clear as if somebody is standing right out in the hallway talking to me. They tell me that I'm a burden. They just keep saying that my family would be better off without me.
